items.title: Meta blocks Malayalam digital media NOCAP’s Facebook page after notice
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Meta India has banned the Facebook page of NOCAP, an independent Malayalam digital media organisation in Kerala. According to NOCAP, Meta has explained that the action was taken based on a notice, citing “unlawful activity.” The page was blocked following a notice, said to be issued by the Government of India/Law Enforcement to Meta under Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, 2000. It is unclear which law enforcement agency or government including the Union and state governments the notice is from. Ali Hyder, the executive editor of NOCAP, said neither Meta nor the government has so far provided a clear explanation as to which specific content published by NOCAP was deemed “unlawful.” Ali Hyder added that attempts are being made in Kerala to control media organisations and digital platforms that raise voices of dissent against the government through various means. “In this context, the action against NOCAP must be examined seriously,” he said. “NOCAP seeks to use journalism to uphold constitutional values and remain firmly rooted in democratic and secular principles. Listen and follow on YouTube Listen and follow on Apple Listen and follow on Spotify Pooja begins the conversation by asking Dr Prabhakar about the Indian Express investigation into the Election Commission and the response issued by the poll body. items.title: TV Newsance 353: Delhi to Mumbai, everyone wants Gyanesh gone
items.summary: This week on TV Newsance, the streets of Delhi and Mumbai were louder than any prime-time debate. The Cockroach Janta Party’s big contribution to the movement against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was “Gyanesh, it’s done bro.” Meanwhile, Delhi University’s women, out on the streets for women's safety, dropped rhymes that made the men’s slogans look like a draft. Poetry round: Women, 1. Boys, 0. So what lit the match? The Indian Express got hold of the Election Commission’s internal file notings, and they show that the other two commissioners were deeply uncomfortable with how the voter-roll revamp, or SIR, was being run.
